messages:
Morgan (PM): Heads-up: aligning scope for Q3 private delivery — need to finalize canary lanes + customer-managed networking acceptance criteria. Customers pushing for non-disruptive upgrades. TL;DR: propose 2-stage canary (internal -> pilot customer) + a 'network-conservative' packaging preset. Thoughts?

Raj (packaging): Agree. Must include IP preservation and a sidecar-less mode for airgapped installs. Also need a clear rollback window in the installer.

Sophie (field): From field: pilot customers want zero-touch DNS handoff. Can we offer a dns-proxy option that preserves external names? Many customers refuse DNS changes.

Alex (eng-runtime): dns-proxy doable but adds ops surface. Alternative: installer writes /etc/hosts + cert SAN mapping for apps that rely on fixed names. That is simpler for pilots.

Morgan (PM): Noted. Draft acceptance criteria idea: successful in-place upgrade where a stateful model process runs >24h post-upgrade and end-to-end request failure delta <= 5% during cutover.

Jen (deploy): Can we standardize canary traffic splits? I propose 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 30m with healthchecks every 2m and automatic rollback on >3 failing healthchecks.

Tim (infra): We have hosted rollout infra but need to port orchestration to private control plane; that's the hairy bit. Need a lightweight shim that speaks to the customer's kube/installer.

Leah (security): :thumbsup: Also flag customer-managed KMS — must include key-rotation test and a documented fallback if rotation fails mid-upgrade.

Raj (packaging): Installer should support a 'network-conservative' preset: avoid changing MTU, do not reconfigure CNI, and preserve existing routing tables. That will reduce field friction.

Morgan (PM): Proposal: two packaging presets — network-conservative and performance-default. network-conservative avoids kernel/CNI changes; perf-default applies all optimizations (MTU, CNI, NIC tuning). Which teams need to sign off?

Sophie (field): Field eng + security + install eng. I can coordinate signoff with ACME pilot and Beta-3 by next Tue.

Alex (eng-runtime): Rough estimate: 2 sprints to implement network-conservative packaging hook + basic canary orchestration shim. Example shim config we could expose to customers:

```
canary:
  steps: [internal, pilot]
  traffic: [5, 95]
  health_check_interval: 120s
  rollback_on: [latency_p95_increase, error_rate]
```

Jen (deploy): We'll need telemetry: surface token-latency and tail errors per customer during canary in Console. Also a canary timeline view.

oncall-bot: Reminder: create incident runbook for failed private canary cutover — template path: /runbooks/private-canary-cutover.

Morgan (PM): Action items: 1) Draft acceptance criteria doc by Fri (Morgan). 2) Eng-runtime: prototype canary shim (Alex). 3) Packaging: add 'network-conservative' flag to installer (Raj). 4) Field: line up 2 pilots (Sophie). Add any missing items.

Tim (infra): Missing: upgrade rollback test harness for large KV caches — add a synthetic load test that simulates 10k concurrent sessions.

Leah (security): Add: KMS fallback test and documented recovery steps; also include threat model for dns-proxy option.

Morgan (PM): Good catches. I'll add both to the acceptance doc. If no objections I'll lock scope EOD tomorrow. :eyes: 

Raj (packaging): One more ask from field: provide an explicit installer flag to force 'preserve-ip' behavior for customers doing provider-managed NAT.

Sophie (field): Also request: a small concierge checklist for netops teams at the customer to run pre-cutover (IP ranges, ACLs, certs). I can draft.

Alex (eng-runtime): I'll mock up the shim and a minimal API for customer-confirmation callbacks (approve/reject) so pilots can opt-in to each stage.

Jen (deploy): I'll add canary metrics to the dashboard backlog and mark it high priority for Q3.

Morgan (PM): Thanks team. If anyone wants to be added to the signoff list ping me. Closing thread after acceptance doc is uploaded.
